chief_complaint: Uncontrolled hypertension with chronic kidney disease and chronic pain
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 55-year-old man with a longstanding history of type 2 diabetes, obesity, and prior NSTEMI (2011). Since 2020 he has progressive chronic kidney disease (stage 3) with proteinuria and microalbuminuria. Blood pressure remains markedly elevated (152/110 mmHg) despite a three‑drug antihypertensive regimen. He reports persistent fibromyalgia and chronic low‑back pain, managed with high‑dose opioid therapy (hydrocodone ER and oxycodone/acetaminophen). Socially, he has limited contact and works full‑time, which may impede self‑care. Recent labs lack updated eGFR, lipid panel, and BMI, limiting assessment of disease control.

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include prior severe anxiety/panic, gingivitis and gingival disease, reports of environmental violence, intimate partner abuse, and periods of part‑time or no employment. risk_factor_summary: Patient has stage 2 hypertension (152/110 mmHg), CKD stage 3, obesity (BMI missing but BMI>30 documented), normal recent A1c (5.6%). Charlson comorbidity index 2 and high clinical complexity. Organ systems at elevated risk: cardiovascular (prior MI, uncontrolled HTN, dyslipidemia), renal (CKD, proteinuria), metabolic (obesity, diabetes), musculoskeletal/pain (fibromyalgia, chronic opioid use), and mental health/social (limited support). Polypharmacy risk is moderate.

eGFR not recorded; essential for CKD staging and medication dosing

clinical_impression: The patient presents with uncontrolled hypertension, stage 3 CKD, and chronic pain requiring high‑dose opioids, compounded by prior myocardial infarction and obesity. Cardiovascular and renal risks are high, and missing key laboratory data (eGFR, lipid panel, BMI) limit optimal management. Polypharmacy is moderate but several agents are critical for risk reduction.
